$comment: One answer-grading fixture set, run by web (vitest), Deno, iOS (Swift Kit) and Android (JVM core). Each case has kind, input and expected. runtimes (optional) lists where a case applies: absent means all four of web, deno, ios, android; typo-verdict and confusion exist only on web and deno. Every runtime a case applies to must produce `expected`; there is no per-runtime exception. Do not edit the native copies (ios/LearnWithAlphonsoKit/Tests/LearnWithAlphonsoKitTests/Fixtures and android/LearnWithAlphonso/core/src/test/resources) by hand: copy this file over them, because guard tests fail when they differ.

cases.note: the oe ligature is not decomposed by NFD and is then stripped as punctuation, so 'coeur' never matches; every runtime agrees
unlike speak, the typed translate path has no French elision join: 'jai' vs 'j ai'
a missing tilde is a forgivable slip (many keyboards have no enye) unless the tilde-less form is a different real word (see the twin cases below)
una (a/one) is a different real word from uña (nail)
pena (pity) is a different real word from peña
manana is not a Spanish word, so the dropped tilde is a slip
Written Spanish keeps the enye: ano (anus) is a different word from año, so the local match refuses it and the AI grader decides; every runtime agrees
capital enye, and the n + combining tilde spelling a phone keyboard can produce
only the enye is protected: acute accents and the inverted marks still fold
